sb_prompt: DISCUSS PLANNING A FAMILY REUNION.  DRAW ON YOUR EXPERIENCES AND THOSE OF THE OTHER CALLER FOR MAKING THE NEXT GET-TOGETHER SUCCESSFUL AND MEMORABLE.
turns: So you're a bus driver? That's funny, my cousin's son is too, but he dropped out of high school and now he hates it because he can't afford to fix his old bus anymore.
Yeah, that's exactly why I stopped driving my niece's bus last year; the parts just got too expensive and she's gotta drive her own car now.

That's rough. But hey, I can't relate to that money problem since I'm stuck working in a cubicle, but my own family reunion last summer was a total disaster because nobody agreed on where to go, so I'm thinking we just need to make the location a big part of the planning this time so no one gets left out.

Yeah, that makes sense, but honestly I'm pretty skeptical about spending tons of money on a fancy venue because my mom tried that once and half the family just stayed home in their pajamas, so maybe keeping it local and cheap is the only way to actually get everyone there.
Yeah, but my cousin's family has this huge house in the suburbs that's basically free to use, so maybe we could just do potluck style there instead of renting a hall?
Right, that actually sounds way more realistic than renting a hall, since my aunt stayed home last time because the hotel was too fancy anyway.
That'd be great, honestly, cause I'd never have to worry about the cost or nobody feeling awkward about paying for food again.
Yeah, plus my own family lives in three different states so driving is a nightmare if it's too far away anyway.
That would solve the travel headache, plus you could just tell people to bring their own sleeping bags if they're bringing kids and saving money on hotels.
Yeah, sleeping bags would be a great idea, actually, since my kid's already got a tent set up in the backyard anyway.
Yeah, and I can make a spreadsheet for everyone to vote on dates and who's cooking what before anyone even commits to spending a dime.
Oh, a spreadsheet? That might be a bit much for my mom, she'd probably just ignore it, but we could at least put it in a group chat so people can vote without me having to chase them down.
Yeah, a group chat sounds way easier than sending twenty separate emails, and then we can just pick the top three dates and see what fits best for everyone.
Yeah, that'd probably work, but I bet she'd just forget to post it and everyone would just guess, which leads to all that confusion about who's bringing what.
Right, but then you just have to rely on them remembering to post it, which usually means the whole thing falls apart and everyone ends up calling me to ask who's bringing the potato salad again.
Yeah, that's exactly what happened with my brother-in-law last time, he got the whole thing wrong so nobody showed up until the third week of August and it was freezing.
Yeah, I had that same problem with my aunt, she always forgot to bring her dish so my cousin ended up buying frozen pizza just so we didn't starve.
Yeah, freezing pizza just isn't gonna cut it for everyone's kids, plus I think if we just let people pick what they want to bring we won't end up with three different brands of chips again.
Yeah, that's the worst part when you have to pay for the chips, nobody ever brings the same brand and it looks like a mess on the table.
Yeah, that's the thing, we could just make a big list of categories and ask people to sign up for one specific thing so we don't end up with five kinds of dip again.
Yeah, that'd be perfect, we could just put categories like "main dish," "salad," and "dessert" and have people claim one before they even start cooking.
Yeah, that sounds like a solid plan, just make sure to put it in the chat so we can actually track who signed up for what.
Yeah, I'll make sure to pin the chat open on my phone so everyone can just check it off and we don't end up with a mess.
Right, but you're gonna have to fight the stubborn aunties who think they're experts at everything, otherwise someone's gonna try to make their own dip and ruin it.
Yeah, I know what you mean, those stubborn aunties are the worst, but I guess we can just tell them to bring a whole main dish if they insist on being the chef.
Yeah, but then you just have to make sure those aunties don't try to make the dip anyway, or we're gonna end up with a whole table of conflicting flavors that nobody wants.
Yeah, that's a real pain, but maybe we can just have a big potluck where everyone brings a main and the aunties bring the sides so we don't end up with three different dips again.
Yeah, if we let them pick their own sides they'll definitely end up with five different dips again, so maybe the aunties just pick a main dish and the rest of us can handle the sides.
Yeah, maybe we just tell everyone to bring something with meat or something so we don't end up with five kinds of chips and nobody gets to eat the stuff they like.
Yeah, that sounds like a solid compromise, just make sure the meat is actually cooked and not raw before we get there.
Yeah, just make sure whoever brings the meat brings it actually cooked so nobody has to ask questions at the dinner table.
Yeah, I'd be worried if someone brought raw chicken and nobody said anything until dinner was half over.
Yeah, just make sure they bring it in a coolert or something and that it's not gonna explode in the trunk of the car.

Right, yeah, I've got a cooler at the back that could keep it safe, but maybe we should just make it a rule that anything with meat has to come fully cooked, otherwise someone's gonna get sick and ruin the whole trip.
Yeah, but how about we just tell everyone to bring whatever's on sale at the grocery store that week so we don't even have to worry about shopping lists?
Yeah, that's a good idea, but honestly I think we should just make it a rule that people bring whatever is already in their own freezer or fridge so we don't have to go shopping at all.
That's the only way to make sure everyone brings something edible without us buying a mountain of frozen pizza.
Yeah, but then how are we gonna figure out who's bringing what if we don't even ask them beforehand?
That's true, but if you don't ask ahead, you're just gonna end up with three people bringing Tater Tot casseroles and nobody bringing anything with corn in it.
Yeah, well just tell them to bring what they're hungry for and I'll do my best to sort it out when things get chaotic.
